title: Anticoagulated de novo atrial flutter complicated by transitory ischemic attack in fatal COVID‐19
case_prompt: A 78-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension, vascular leukoencephalopathy, and coronary heart disease was admitted for COVID-19 and treated with oxygen and steroids. On hospital day 2, he developed de novo atrial flutter, and therapeutic enoxaparin was started after myocardial infarction was excluded by ECG and absence of chest pain. On hospital day 5, he had sudden-onset right-sided hemiparesis (NIHSS score 7) with spontaneous, complete recovery within 24 hours. Cerebral MRI, including time-of-flight angiography, showed no acute lesion. He was diagnosed with a transient ischemic attack, and anticoagulation was continued. A nonconvulsive epileptic seizure was considered, and levetiracetam 2,000 mg/day was initiated; on hospital day 7, although seizure-free, the dose was increased to 3,000 mg/day.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Cardioembolic TIA from atrial flutter was considered — “The cause of the TIA remained speculative but most likely it was due to newly detected atrial flutter or the hypercoagulability syndrome.”  
2. Hypercoagulability syndrome was considered due to COVID-19 — “An indication for hypercoagulability in the index patient was the mildly elevated D-dimer.”  
3. Small-vessel cerebrovascular disease from diabetes or hypertension was considered but imaging was unrevealing — “Alternative causes of TIA could be cerebro-vascular disease due to diabetes or arterial hypertension…However, cerebral MRI…were non-informative.”  
4. Focal nonconvulsive seizure was considered but EEG showed no epileptiform discharges — “a self-limiting, non-convulsive epileptic state was considered…however, EEG on hd20 only showed diffuse generalized slowing without epileptiform discharges and without ever having experienced a seizure.”  
5. Direct SARS-CoV-2 CNS involvement was considered but CSF investigations were noninformative — “Alternative causes…a cerebral manifestation of the SARS-CoV-2 infection. However, cerebral MRI, CSF investigations, and EEG were non-informative.”
